title: Auth Control Plane user access token (v1 wire format)
description:
The user access token the auth-service signs (credential class `user_access_token`, TRD section 11): a compact JWS whose protected header and payload, decoded, are the two members of this document. The signature is not part of the document; a verifier checks it with the issuer's jwks.v1 key named by `kid` BEFORE it reads the claims.

WHAT A SCHEMA CAN SAY. The header is exactly {alg EdDSA, typ at+jwt, kid}: no symmetric algorithm, no `none`, and no member that moves key selection out of the verifier's hands (jku, jwk, x5u, x5c, crit). The claims are a closed set: identity and session only. role, email, username, full_name, is_superuser, tv and the HS256 token's `type` are not in it; authorization is checked live per request. `aud` is one string, never an array. `scope` is a closed vocabulary bound to the audience.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY, AND THE CLIENT RULES THAT CLOSE IT. JSON Schema cannot compare two members, so internal/auth/contracts ParseAccessToken holds these rules, pinned by the manifest's `reject_by_client` fixtures, which are valid against this schema on purpose:
  1. iat <= nbf < exp.
  2. exp - iat is at most the HS256-compat ceiling, AccessTokenLifetimeCeiling in internal/auth/contracts.
  3. A duplicate member in the header or the claims is refused, before any other check.
  4. iat, nbf and exp are integer tokens; a decimal form is refused.

header.description: The JWS protected header. Closed: a verifier never reads a key, key URL or certificate from the token.

alg.description: Ed25519 only (ACP-ADR-01). A verifier fixes this before it resolves a key.

typ.description: RFC 9068 access-token type. It separates this token from an ID token, a workload token and the HS256 token, which carries typ JWT.

claims.description: The JWT claims. Closed to identity and session: nothing in it grants a permission.

aud.description: Exactly one audience. dev-health-api is go-api and query-api (REST and /query); auth-service is its own session routes. contracts/auth/v1/vocabulary/audiences.json lists every audience and the class that may carry it.

principal_type.description: A user access token names a human principal. Workload tokens are another class.

org_id.description: The organization the session acts in, as a lowercase UUID. Absent means no organization; there is no null form. A relying party re-checks membership; this claim is context, not proof.

scope.description: Coarse scope, bound to the audience: api:access with dev-health-api, auth:session with auth-service. Closed: an unknown scope is refused.

numericDate.description: Seconds since the epoch (RFC 7519 NumericDate), no later than 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z.
